analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, patches and supplied source against the indexed threat model and selected T-041 detail. No concrete security regression is established in this scope. The composite action defaults cache writes off and gates Swift, Metal and new SwiftPM repository saves on explicit caller permission (.github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml:7–9,107,116,143). ci.yml supplies that permission only for master/dev push events (head:19 and patch:267,510,706,1044,1106), reducing PR cache writes. New dependency cache keys bind OS, workspace/home layout, lane and lockfiles; fallback restoration still relies on SwiftPM resolution, whose implementation was not examined.

The workflow adds daily .git restoration across jobs, connectivity checks before checkout, and saves immediately after checkout with persist-credentials:false (ci.yml patch head:58–94 and repeated blocks). This creates a metadata-cache trust contract: git fsck checks connectivity, not configuration, hooks or producer authenticity. The shown writers are push-gated and precede repository test execution; there is no supplied evidence of an adversarial writer to a cache scope consumed by trusted jobs, so cache poisoning is not reported as a vulnerability. Full-history Docs checkout uses a separate cache family and blob filtering; other checkouts omit only specified evidence archives and landing media. Cluster key normalization retains submodule commit/path identity while dropping descriptive refs (patch head:923).

Integration should reconcile the new mimo_audio classifier contract: fixture preparation now requires needs.changes.outputs.mimo_audio (ci.yml patch head:404,412), which indirectly controls the existing native audio-release gate (base:307–314). Examine scripts/ci-component-paths.py and component-changes.yml changes to ensure all audio admission/release dependencies trigger the gate and master pushes retain it; their source is absent here. This affects TB-007 availability/admission assurance, not evidence of a runtime bypass. CI caches are distinct from T-041 consumer KV storage; no supplied change alters encryption, tenant scoping, authorization, attestation, billing or plaintext handling.
